question_text: To whom is a high impact cost beneficial?
solution_text: A high impact cost increases the buying price and reduces the selling price, making it disadvantageous to both buyers and sellers.

question_text: Initial margin to be paid in derivatives is set up taking into account the volatility of the underlying market. Generally
option_a: Lower the volatility, higher the initial margin
option_b: Higher the volatility, lower the initial margin
option_c: Higher the volatility, higher the initial margin
solution_text: Higher volatility implies greater risk; hence, higher margins are imposed to safeguard traders and members.

question_text: _______ is the ratio of change in option premium for a unit change in volatility.
solution_text: Vega measures the sensitivity of the option premium to changes in market volatility.

question_text: In a derivatives exchange the networth requirement for a clearing member is higher than that of a non-clearing member - State whether True or False?
solution_text: Clearing members bear more responsibility and must maintain a higher net worth.

question_text: The risk that cannot be controlled by diversification of portfolio is
solution_text: Systematic risk affects the entire market and cannot be eliminated through diversification.

question_text: Can a long position in a Put option be closed out by taking a short position in a call option with identical exercise date and exercise price?
solution_text: A long Put position must be closed by selling the same Put, not by taking a Call position.

question_text: After the initiation of the futures contract the price of the underlying asset has risen. In this situation
option_a: Price change in underlying has no effect on positions
solution_text: A rise in the underlying price benefits the buyer (long position) of the futures.

question_text: There are many products in the market which give high returns in a risk-free manner - True or False?
solution_text: Higher returns are generally associated with higher risks. No product gives high returns risk-free.

question_text: What will be the Delta for a Far Out-of-the-money option?
solution_text: Far OTM options have very low probability of ending in-the-money, thus Delta nears zero.

question_text: The term mark-to-market means
option_d: Daily revaluation of open positions by the exchange
solution_text: MTM adjusts positions to reflect daily gains/losses based on market prices.

question_text: The margining system for index futures is based on
solution_text: Index futures margins are calculated using VAR methodology at 99% confidence level.

question_text: Mr. Ashu has bought 100 shares of ABC at Rs 980 per share and doesn't want to lose more than Rs 1000. What should he do?
solution_text: A Rs 10 drop would result in Rs 1000 loss on 100 shares. Hence stop loss at Rs 970.

question_text: A call option gives the buyer the right to buy the underlying at market price - True or False?
solution_text: A call option gives the right to buy at the strike price, not the market price.

question_text: A trader buys a Jan ABC futures contract at Rs 768 (lot size 1200) and squares off at Rs 778. What is the profit/loss?
solution_text: Profit per share = Rs 10 x 1200 = Rs 12000.

question_text: A Professional Clearing Member of the derivatives segment
option_a: Must be a cash segment member
solution_text: PCMs provide clearing services but cannot trade on the exchange.

question_text: Theta is a measure of the sensitivity of an option price to changes in market volatility - True or False?
solution_text: Theta measures sensitivity to time decay; Vega measures sensitivity to volatility.

question_text: Which of these complaints against a trading member can an Exchange redress?
solution_text: Exchanges can address unauthorized trading, margin shortfalls, delay in settlement, etc.

question_text: In India the clearing and settlement of derivatives trades is done through:
option_c: SEBI approved Clearing Corporation / Clearing House
solution_text: Clearing of F&O trades is handled by SEBI-approved clearing corporations.

question_text: Delta is the change in option price given a one percentage point change in the risk-free interest rate - True or False?
solution_text: Rho measures sensitivity to interest rates. Delta is sensitivity to the underlying price.

question_text: Can a Clearing Member give 'Fixed Deposits' as part of liquid assets to the Clearing Corporation?
solution_text: Fixed Deposits are acceptable as part of liquid assets along with cash and approved securities.

question_text: Vega measures change in delta with respect to change in price of the underlying asset - True or False?
solution_text: Vega measures sensitivity to volatility. Gamma measures change in Delta.

question_text: A short position in a PUT option can be closed out by taking a long position in the same PUT option - True or False?
solution_text: Opposite positions in the same contract (same strike/date) offset each other.

question_text: On final settlement the buyer/holder of the option will recognize the favorable difference received from the seller/writer as _______ in the profit and loss account.
solution_text: Any favorable payoff is treated as income in the books of the option holder.

question_text: Higher the strike price the premium on call option will decrease - True or False?
solution_text: Higher strike prices make options less valuable (lower intrinsic value), reducing premiums.

question_text: Trading is allowed in Indian equity markets in which of the following?
solution_text: All three instruments are actively traded in Indian derivatives markets.

question_text: Can the exercise price be more than or equal to or less than the cash spot price?
solution_text: The strike (exercise) price is fixed for an options contract, while the spot price can fluctuate. Therefore, the exercise price can be greater than, equal to, or less than the cash spot price.

question_text: Can one sell assets in futures market even if he does not own any such assets?
solution_text: In futures markets, short-selling is allowed even without owning the underlying asset, as delivery is not mandatory and positions are usually squared off before expiry.

question_text: On the derivatives futures market if there are three series of one two and three months open at a point of time how many calendar spread can one have?
solution_text: Calendar spreads are possible between (1-2), (2-3), and (1-3) month contracts. Hence, three combinations are possible.

question_text: All the 50 stocks of NSE Nifty index are equally weighed while calculating the index - State True or False?
solution_text: Nifty 50 is calculated using the free-float market capitalization method so stocks are not equally weighted.

question_text: What does a Call Option give the buyer?
option_a: The right but not the obligation
option_b: The obligation but not the right
option_c: Gives both the right and obligation
option_d: Neither the right nor the obligation
solution_text: A call option gives the buyer the right (but not the obligation) to buy the underlying asset at the strike price before or at expiry.

question_text: Speculators are those who take risk whereas hedgers are those who wish to reduce risk - State True or False?
solution_text: Hedgers aim to minimize risk from adverse price movements, while speculators take on risk in hopes of making profit from market movements.

question_text: The money and securities which are deposited in a client's account
option_a: Can be attached for meeting broker's obligations
option_b: Cannot be attached for meeting broker's obligations
option_c: Can or cannot be attached depending on clearing corporation
solution_text: Client funds and securities are kept in separate accounts and cannot be used to meet the broker's proprietary obligations.

question_text: In case there is a Stock Split of a company which is a part of an Index what will its impact be on the index value?
solution_text: A stock split affects share price and quantity but not the market capitalization, hence index value remains unaffected.

question_text: 'Time Decay' is beneficial to the
solution_text: As time passes, the time value of options erodes, which benefits the seller since the premium reduces.

question_text: Identify the TRUE statement with respect to a Put option.
option_a: Buyer and seller both have obligations
option_b: Buyer has right to sell to the writer
option_c: Seller has right to buy from the buyer
option_d: Buyer has obligation but not the right
solution_text: A put option gives the buyer the right (not obligation) to sell an asset at a specified price within a timeframe.

question_text: Mr. Menon has bought a futures contract and the price rises. In this case Mr. Menon will
solution_text: Buying a futures contract is a bullish strategy. If the price rises the buyer profits.

question_text: How is the forward contract which is for hedging purpose accounted for in books of accounts?
solution_text: Per AS-11, the forward premium or discount is amortized over the life of the contract if used for hedging.

question_text: A Derivative market helps in transferring the risk from
solution_text: Derivatives enable hedgers to offload their risk to speculators who are willing to take it.

question_text: Which of these options is an example of a Calendar Spread?
option_a: Short underpriced 1-month long overpriced another month
option_c: Long underpriced 1-month short overpriced another month
solution_text: Calendar spreads involve arbitrage between contracts of different expiry months.

question_text: Ms. Kavita wants to 'Sell' on a futures market. For this she
option_c: Must own at least 25% of underlying
option_d: Must own at least 50% of underlying
solution_text: Futures contracts are standardized and traded on margin. Ownership of underlying is not required to sell.

question_text: The Derivatives market helps in
option_a: Transferring risk from low to high risk appetite participants
solution_text: Derivatives help in risk transfer and reallocation, aiding both hedgers and speculators.

question_text: Identify the FALSE statement with respect to Options.
option_b: Buyer gets right seller bears obligation
solution_text: Options have asymmetric and non-linear payoffs. The buyer's risk is limited; the seller's risk can be unlimited.

question_text: 'SCORES' is the name given to
solution_text: SCORES stands for SEBI COmplaints REdress System - a centralized online grievance mechanism.

question_text: A trading member reaches his prescribed position limits. Therefore he will
option_b: Not be able to reverse positions
option_c: Can take fresh positions for clients
option_d: Not be able to open new positions
solution_text: When position limits are breached, no fresh positions are allowed. Only reversal of existing ones is permitted.

question_text: A calendar spread in index futures will be treated as _______ in a far month contract if the near month contract expires.
solution_text: With one leg expired, the spread becomes a single directional or naked position, increasing risk exposure.

question_text: The clearing member is free to close out transactions of a trading member if
solution_text: Clearing members can close out positions if margin or settlement dues are unpaid, to mitigate systemic risk.

question_text: Identify the contract which is cleared and settled bilaterally:
option_c: 3-month forward to buy CHF against INR
solution_text: Forward contracts are over-the-counter and bilateral, unlike exchange-traded futures and options.

question_text: When the volatility of the underlying stock decreases the premium of its Call option will
solution_text: Option premiums are directly proportional to volatility. Lower volatility leads to lower premium.

question_text: A European call option will give the buyer the right (but not the obligation) to buy the underlying at the strike price
option_b: On or before the expiry date
solution_text: European options can only be exercised on the expiry date, unlike American options.

question_text: In futures trading the margin is paid by
solution_text: Both parties to a futures contract must deposit initial margin with the exchange to safeguard against default.
